sources_read: .qc-cache/kittle-2026-10-09-r7/rules/WebDev Rubrics QC.xlsx: Quality Checks row 40 (#39 floor_is_low_for_shells_mocks_and_stuffing), Internal Quality Checks row 40, plus related rows D30/D44
evidence: Walked through all five floor archetypes against the frozen bytes. (1) Blank page / no server: test.sh writes the zero reward first and exits 0 when /app/server.js is missing or HTTP is never ready. The render gate (gates/render/judge.toml:25-33, all_pass, binary) needs a real Kittle & Rowe chat, nothing private before sign-in, the wrong password refused and Gwen's matters/messages shown. (2) Static mock / client-only fake / localStorage seed copy: the constraints gate (gates/constraints/judge.toml:25-37) has Gwen post 'Gate check JUDGE-G1' in M-11, reload, then sign in as Harriet in a separate browser context and see it. Only a server-side write passes this, so static HTML, first-paint seed copies and per-browser storage all fail. score.py:41 requires gates > 0.0, and test.sh exits on gate code 1 before the scored suite runs, so reward = 0. (3) Refuse-everything: the constraints gate needs a successful post, so it fails. Every scored prompt also forbids passing a refusal without its success control ('Every refusal pairs with a success of the same kind', functional prompt.md:51-52), and every functional criterion lists positive controls. (4) Keyword-stuffed: gates and functional criteria grade operations and readbacks, not text. Each scored prompt repeats the gate ('seeded-looking facade ... first-paint imitation does not pass', functional prompt.md:11-19, polish prompt.md:10-18, visual prompt.md:10-18). The visual likert rows (for example retention_marks 'On hold' badges) could reward stuffed text, but the functional floor of 0.05 (scoring.toml [floors]) zeros the reward unless real functional weight > 2.2/44 passes. One 1.5 or 2.0 criterion alone (0.034/0.045) does not clear it, so polish/visual cannot be farmed by a non-working app. (5) A seed-serving server that accepts posts in memory passes the gates legitimately. It is a real backend, not a shell, and still fails persistence and most criteria. Network-public/CDN wording is correct in all five prompts (not a floor case). scoring.toml, score.py and test.sh are byte-identical to the frozen template. Runtime: hosted nop on the previous v2 bytes = 0.0 (gates_passed 0, no_op 1), consistent with case 1, but it is not on this candidate. No configured judge run of a static mock, stuffed or refusing app exists for these bytes (raw-evidence-index scope says discrimination is absent). So the judge's actual behavior on those weak apps is unmeasured, and risk stays true. That is an evidence gap, not a demonstrated defect.
